title: Misaligned invoice credits after regional failover causing doubled token charges
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several customers on Dedicated and Private plans reported unexpected overcharges and missing invoice credits after a regional failover event on 2026-03-03. Root cause appears to be duplicated metering events produced during retry/replica reconvergence combined with an eventual-consistent aggregator that did not deduplicate properly. This ticket tracks the production bugfix, customer reconciliation plan, and follow-up hardening work.
impact: High — 3 enterprise customers reported +10% token billing variance for the last billing period; one customer paused usage and engaged revenue and legal. Public-hosted customers show smaller drift but are not included in the initial escalation list.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate a regional failover with in-flight requests from node-a to node-b
2) Force a client retry with identical request IDs (some retries did not carry idempotency keys)
3) Observe metering-proxy emitting two usage events for the same request to the aggregator
4) Aggregator applies both events because dedup window is misaligned with TTL propagation from edge caches
5) Billing job consumes duplicated aggregates and issues charges/credits accordingly
investigation_summary: On initial triage we confirmed two contributing symptoms: (A) the per-request idempotency header was not consistently set by older SDKs used by a subset of customers and by internal retry logic introduced during failover; (B) the metering-aggregator's dedup index used a Redis key with a 60s TTL, but edge caches were replicating IDs with up to 120s propagation, allowing duplicate events to slip through. Additionally, the billing consumer assumed monotonic aggregates and lacked a secondary dedup step.
root_cause: A combination of inconsistent idempotency headers during failover retries and an aggregator dedup configuration mismatch. The aggregator and edge caches had different expectations for dedup windows, creating a race where duplicates were accepted. Billing pipeline also lacked a final idempotency guard.
mitigation: Short term: (1) Deploy hotfix to metering-proxy to add server-side idempotency key generation when a client header is missing; (2) Temporarily widen aggregator dedup window + make TTL authoritative by using a single leader for the dedup index; (3) Pause automated billing runs for affected customers and disable retro-billing job until reconciliation completes. Long term: implement idempotent billing consumer and canonicalize dedup window across components.
rollback_plan: Hotfix is non-destructive but reversible: rollback metering-proxy to previous image and remove server-side idempotency feature. Aggregator TTL change can be reverted by restoring previous configuration. Billing pause has no rollback (manual resume after reconciliation).
follow_up_tasks: Create SDK patch and migration guide to enforce client-side idempotency headers (PM + DevRel)
Implement robust final dedup in billing-consumer that uses unique request IDs and canonical timestamp window
Add integration tests that simulate cross-region failover and validate no double-counting
Post-incident runbook update: failover metering checklist and communication template for customers
